As a library grows, one giant class becomes hard to navigate. **PythonLibCore**
(the toolkit the Browser library itself is built on) lets you split keywords
across several small classes and compose them into one library.

You inherit from `DynamicCore`, pass it your component instances, and decorate
each keyword method with `@keyword`. The components stay focused; the library
presents them as one flat set of keywords.

## Task 1 — Compose two keyword classes into one library

**Goal:** create `libraries/ShopLibrary.py` — a `ShopLibrary(DynamicCore)` that
composes an `OrderKeywords` component (an `order_reference` keyword) and a
`CartKeywords` component (`add_item_price` and `cart_total`).

Here is the same composition over a different pair of components. Adapt it to
orders and a cart.

<!-- example -->
```python
from robotlibcore import DynamicCore, keyword


class GreetKeywords:
    @keyword
    def greeting_for(self, name):
        return f"Hello, {name}!"


class CountKeywords:
    def __init__(self):
        self.seen = 0

    @keyword
    def count_one(self):
        self.seen += 1

    @keyword
    def times_counted(self) -> int:
        return self.seen


class HelloLibrary(DynamicCore):
    def __init__(self):
        DynamicCore.__init__(self, [GreetKeywords(), CountKeywords()])
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `libraries/ShopLibrary.py` defines a `ShopLibrary` class built on PythonLibCore.

<!-- hint -->
Import from the toolkit: `from robotlibcore import DynamicCore, keyword`. Write two
small component classes, each with `@keyword` methods.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
The main class passes instances of both components up to `DynamicCore`:
`DynamicCore.__init__(self, [OrderKeywords(), CartKeywords()])`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```python
from robotlibcore import DynamicCore, keyword


class OrderKeywords:
    @keyword
    def order_reference(self, prefix, number: int) -> str:
        return f"{prefix}-{number:04d}"


class CartKeywords:
    def __init__(self):
        self.prices = []

    @keyword
    def add_item_price(self, price: float):
        self.prices.append(price)

    @keyword
    def cart_total(self) -> float:
        return sum(self.prices)


class ShopLibrary(DynamicCore):
    def __init__(self):
        DynamicCore.__init__(self, [OrderKeywords(), CartKeywords()])
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Import it and run it green

Create `checks/shop.robot` — keywords from both components are available as one set:

```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    ../libraries/ShopLibrary.py

*** Test Cases ***
One Library Two Components
    ${ref}=    Order Reference    TRN    ${3}
    Should Be Equal    ${ref}    TRN-0003
    Add Item Price    19.90
    Add Item Price    12.00
    ${total}=    Cart Total
    Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${total}    31.90
```

Run it:

```bash
uv run robot checks/shop.robot
```

**Check:** the test `One Library Two Components` passes.
